rationale: Elihu voices a question about what one will do if one sins. Job earlier asked what he could do to God if he sinned; the conditional sin-and-action question corresponds, although Elihu's version does not repeat the explicit object to Thee.

Job places a hand over his mouth when confronted by God's questions. Micah describes nations placing hands over their mouths and fearing the Lord after seeing His wonders; the shared gesture accompanies recognition of divine strength in different subjects.
